scenes.tts: One kind of cell tells you a violin is playing, and that your head just turned toward it. How?
scenes.visual: A violin to the left of a listener's head; the head turns toward it. Question on screen: one cell, hearing and balance?
scenes.narration: One kind of cell tells you a violin is playing, and that your head just turned toward it. How?

scenes.tts: On top of each hair cell sits a bundle of stiff stereocilia, graded in height like a staircase.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the inner ear, then onto one hair cell: a staircase bundle of stereocilia. Label: hair bundle.
scenes.narration: On top of each hair cell sits a bundle of stiff stereocilia, graded in height like a staircase.

scenes.tts: Fine tip links join each shorter one to its taller neighbour.
scenes.visual: Thin threads drawn from each shorter stereocilium's tip to its taller neighbour. Label: tip links (cadherin 23 and protocadherin 15).
scenes.narration: Fine tip links join each shorter one to its taller neighbour.

scenes.tts: At rest, the links carry some tension, so some channels are already open. Here, take a cell with only a few open.
scenes.visual: The bundle upright, nothing pushing. A handful of channels near the tips glow open; most are dark. Label: some open at rest (this example: a few; outer hair cells: nearer half).
scenes.narration: At rest, the links carry some tension, so some channels are already open. Here, take a cell with only a few open.

scenes.tts: Push the bundle toward its tallest stereocilia. The links tighten, more channels open, and the cell depolarizes.
scenes.visual: A probe pushes the bundle toward the tall side. Links tighten; many channels glow. A current meter rises; the voltage trace steps up. Label: depolarizes.
scenes.narration: Push the bundle toward its tallest stereocilia. The links tighten, more channels open, and the cell depolarizes.

scenes.tts: Now push it the other way. What happens to the current?
scenes.visual: The probe moves to the other side of the bundle. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now push it the other way. What happens to the current?

scenes.tts: The few channels open at rest close. Less current flows in, and the cell hyperpolarizes.
scenes.visual: Links go slack; the few glowing channels go dark. The meter dips; the voltage trace steps down. Label: hyperpolarizes.
scenes.narration: The few channels open at rest close. Less current flows in, and the cell hyperpolarizes.

scenes.tts: But the effect is lopsided. There is less room to reduce the current than to increase it, because only the channels open at rest can close.
scenes.visual: An S-shaped curve of transduction conductance, as a fraction of its maximum, against bundle displacement: it rises far on the toward side and flattens soon on the away side. Label: illustrative, small resting open fraction; the voltage response also depends on the cell's other conductances.
scenes.narration: But the effect is lopsided. There is less room to reduce the current than to increase it, because only the channels open at rest can close.

scenes.tts: What carries the current? The hair cell's two ends sit in two different fluids.
scenes.visual: The cell set into a wall. Top region shaded and labelled endolymph; bottom region labelled perilymph.
scenes.narration: What carries the current? The hair cell's two ends sit in two different fluids.

scenes.tts: The top faces endolymph. It is rich in potassium, and in the cochlea it is held about eighty millivolts positive.
scenes.caption: The top faces endolymph. It is rich in K⁺, and in the cochlea it is held about +80 mV positive.
scenes.visual: Potassium dots crowded above the cell and inside it. Labels: endolymph, K⁺-rich; about +80 mV (endocochlear potential), made by the cochlea's wall.
scenes.narration: The top faces endolymph. It is rich in K⁺, and in the cochlea it is held about +80 mV positive.

scenes.tts: The base faces perilymph, which is low in potassium.
scenes.caption: The base faces perilymph, which is low in K⁺.
scenes.visual: Few potassium dots below the cell. Label: perilymph, low K⁺, high Na⁺.
scenes.narration: The base faces perilymph, which is low in K⁺.

scenes.tts: Across the top, the inside is far more negative than the endolymph. So potassium is pushed in, hard.
scenes.caption: Across the top, the inside is far more negative than the endolymph. So K⁺ is pushed in, hard.
scenes.visual: Labels: endolymph +80 mV, cell inside −50 mV (illustrative, both against perilymph). An arrow: K⁺ in at the top. Label: push about 130 mV.
scenes.narration: Across the top, the inside is far more negative than the endolymph. So K⁺ is pushed in, hard.

scenes.tts: Across the base, potassium leaves through potassium channels. In this steady picture, as much leaves as enters.
scenes.caption: Across the base, K⁺ leaves through potassium channels. In this steady picture, as much leaves as enters.
scenes.visual: An arrow of the same width as the top one: K⁺ out at the base, through K⁺ channels, into perilymph. Label: steady, K⁺-dominated two-current approximation; about 130 mV drive at the top and 40 mV at the base, so equal flow needs about 3.25 times as much total basal conductance.
scenes.narration: Across the base, K⁺ leaves through potassium channels. In this steady picture, as much leaves as enters.

scenes.tts: So potassium runs downhill the whole way. The battery is in the wall of the cochlea, not in the cell.
scenes.caption: So K⁺ runs downhill the whole way. The battery is in the wall of the cochlea, not in the cell.
scenes.visual: Potassium dots stream in at the top and out at the base in one path. A battery icon appears in the cochlea's wall. Label: the battery is in the wall.
scenes.narration: So K⁺ runs downhill the whole way. The battery is in the wall of the cochlea, not in the cell.

scenes.tts: The cell's voltage settles where two pulls balance. Open transduction channels pull it up.
scenes.visual: A voltage scale from about −90 mV to about +80 mV with a marker for the cell. Upper rope labelled transduction channels, toward about +80 mV. Label: steady two-conductance cartoon, no injected or other current.
scenes.narration: The cell's voltage settles where two pulls balance. Open transduction channels pull it up.

scenes.tts: Basal potassium channels pull it down. Moving the bundle changes the top pull directly.
scenes.visual: Lower rope labelled basal K⁺ channels, toward about −90 mV. The bundle tips; the upper rope thickens and the marker slides up. Note: steady state, no injected or other current, qualitative; real basal conductances vary with voltage.
scenes.narration: Basal potassium channels pull it down. Moving the bundle changes the top pull directly.

scenes.tts: Depolarization opens calcium channels at the base, and calcium entry drives transmitter release onto the nerve fibre.
scenes.visual: Calcium channels at the base open; vesicles at a ribbon synapse release onto an afferent fibre. Label: mature cochlear hair cell, graded release; spikes start in the nerve fibre.
scenes.narration: Depolarization opens calcium channels at the base, and calcium entry drives transmitter release onto the nerve fibre.

scenes.tts: So a hair cell's first response reports which way, and how far, its bundle is pushed.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: a hair cell reports which way, and how far, its bundle is pushed. Small label: initial response; adaptation and membrane dynamics shape it over time.
scenes.narration: So a hair cell's first response reports which way, and how far, its bundle is pushed.

scenes.tts: What that means depends on what pushes the bundle, and on the circuits that read the cell.
scenes.visual: The card adds two arrows: mechanics in front (what pushes which bundle), circuits behind (where, when, which side).
scenes.narration: What that means depends on what pushes the bundle, and on the circuits that read the cell.
